text: Yes. Thank you very much, Your Worship. We're looking at the Council, you may recall, ratified the General Insurance Risk Management Services Agreement with BFL and BFL Canada Risk and Insurance Incorporated in 2017. The term of that insurance was for four years. And the appointment expires March the 31st, 2021. Typically, we would move out to a request for proposals sometime in early January 2021 for coverage for April 1, 2021. You can see my discussion that I've put out some facts and figures are related to insurance over the past couple of years and how it affects municipalities in that municipalities are seeing more weather-related losses as the reality of climate change means a more unpredictable and volatile weather patterns. Municipalities also are plagued by adverse claim trends in the municipal sector, increasing damage rewards and class action lawsuits. Our liability and premiums increased in 2021 as a result of increased cost of claim settlement for Canadian municipalities and adverse claims development for the town. Presently, the town has several outstanding liability claims with our current provider, which must be disclosed as part of a request for proposal process. And in addition, we don't know the extent to which COVID-19 pandemic and other catastrophic environmental events in this past year will affect the supply of municipal insurance. And we know that insurance companies for all sectors have put stricter rules in place regarding the amount and breadth of coverage that they will provide and to which clients because the supply of insurance is reduced and the demand for insured capacity is increasing and as such, prices are elevating. In 2019 and 2020, insurance carriers have disappeared with JTL being purchased by Marsh and the Frank Cowan Company was purchased as part of an acquisition by Intact Insurance. It is not known at this time how transactions will affect the market. Because of several uncertain factors, it may be prudent for the town to extend its affiliation with BFL Canada for one more year, at least until the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic have begun to stabilize. BFL Canada is open to a continued relationship with the town in 2021 and it does not anticipate issues as to the choice of limits, values and types of coverage. Based on recent municipal renewals just booked by BFL, I'm told that the premiums have increased. BFL anticipates about a 10% increase on property, including inflationary and value increases, about a 30 to 40% increase on the auto portion and 10 to 15% on liability. However, who knows what the next few months are going to bring. We are all in uncharted territory. Translating the maximum anticipated pricing increases to the town's 2021 premium, as an estimate, the net increase by fund could be as follows. The town of Kentville would pay an additional $24,200. The sanitary sewer operating fund would pay additional $2,300 and the water utility operating would pay an additional $3,900. Total increase would be around $30,400 overall. This would bring our insurance premium from our 2021 figure of in total $166,402 to somewhere around $196,800, which sounds like a huge increase. But I want council to be aware that in 2016-17, when we were with McDonald Trask Limited and Frank Cowan, our premium that year was $196,000. So we're still below what we would have paid Frank Cowan in 2016-17. BSL pricing over the life of the contract has ranged in the early days. The first year we were at around $94,165. We've moved upwards in years two and three. In year three, it was $117,558. And in the year 2020, it moved upwards to $166,400. And that's purely related to all the things that are going on in the world, related to me to litigation, the wildfires flooding worldwide, let alone all the municipal lawsuits and class action suits that have been affecting not only municipalities, but the world overall. So my recommendation to Council Advisory Committee is that I recommend to Council Advisory Committee that the Town of Kentville extend its relationship with BSL for general insurance and risk management services for one year, April 1, 2021 to March 31st, 2022.
